clue.text: Fat fellow with dog getting past

parts.note: a lab is a Labrador retriever
by can mean past, as in walking by the house

explanation.surface: A portly man walks his dog along the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both describe someone soft and carrying too much weight.

clue.text: Musical genre, loud and no good, receiving ugly looks

indicators.note: the loud and no-good letters take in the other piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: ugly suggests the letters of looks are distorted

explanation.surface: A noisy, poor style of music gets dirty looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ugly' looks like a description of the looks, but it is the anagram signal; the mixed-up letters sit between the loud and no-good letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: traditional song of the people is a recognised style of music.

clue.text: Increase millions invested by chap chasing gold

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the chap piece follows gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: the millions are put inside the chap, as money is invested in someone

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman or chap
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A fortune-hunter pursuing gold gets millions put into him, boosting his wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to augment is to add to or make larger.

clue.text: Minor component had effect: reduced pressure level

parts.note: bit is the past of bite, to take effect, as when brakes bite
P is pressure cut down to its abbreviation
a layer is a level or stratum

explanation.surface: A small part made a difference once the pressure was turned down a notch.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an actor with a tiny role, so a person of small part in something.

clue.text: Film trophy concealed by men

parts.note: to palm something is to hide it in the hand, as a conjuror does
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An award is smuggled out of sight by a group of men.
explanation.walkthrough: The trophy is the top prize at the Cannes Film Festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Cannes festival's golden palm is its highest cinema award.

clue.text: Excellent place for boxing trophy, on table in warm spot

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
boxers fight in a ring
a cup is a trophy
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A top spot to keep a boxing prize is on a table in a heated corner.
explanation.walkthrough: An airing cupboard is a British household cupboard round the hot-water tank where laundry is dried.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the heated closet housing a hot-water tank, a cosy place in a home.

clue.text: Parrot about to fill stomach

indicators.note: about goes inside the stomach, filling it

parts.note: maw is the stomach or gullet of an animal
ca, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A bird is about to eat its fill.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large, brightly coloured tropical American parrot.

clue.text: Satisfied about a male with acceptable suit component

indicators.note: the word for satisfied goes around the other pieces

parts.note: did can mean satisfied or sufficed, as in that did me
on means acceptable, as in that's not on

explanation.surface: Content with a man wearing a respectable suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing; it is a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the four card suits, so a card of that set.

clue.text: Hint the writer's mostly in debt?

indicators.note: the shortened word for the writer's goes inside the debt word

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt

indicators.note: mostly means losing the last letter

parts.note: the writer refers to themselves, so the writer's is mine

explanation.surface: A suggestion that the author is largely broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: to prompt or jog the memory, giving a nudge.

clue.text: Clothing manufacturer scrapped torn material ripped apart by chief

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are split open with the chief piece inside
scrapped suggests the letters of torn material are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A tailor throws out torn cloth that the boss tore apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrapped' gives MERANTTAILOR from the two fodder words; 'ripped apart by' splits it after its third letter for the chief's two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic term for a tailor who also sold cloth, as in the London livery company.

clue.text: Long distance to go? Not a time for heavy activity?

definitions.meaning: an astronomical unit of length, how far light travels in twelve months

definitions.text: Not a time for heavy activity?
definitions.meaning: read playfully as a twelvemonth with little work in it

explanation.surface: Someone facing a long trip wonders whether this is a year to take it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: The astronomical unit is a huge span; the whimsical second reading is a year of gentle effort.

clue.text: Constant abuse will do for attraction

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
to abuse someone is to do them harm

explanation.surface: Persistent mistreatment will kill off any appeal someone has.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: allure or appeal that draws people in.

clue.text: Ambassador involved in appeals about matter of record?

indicators.note: the ambassador is wrapped up within the appeals, so one piece sits inside the other
about signals that the word for appeals is turned round

parts.note: calls are appeals or requests
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A diplomat is caught up in pleas over some matter on file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes SLLAC. The question mark warns that 'record' means a gramophone disc, not a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Old 78 rpm gramophone discs were made of this resin, so it is literally the stuff records were pressed from.

clue.text: Submariner prepared to receive onset of water in dark period

indicators.note: the submariner and prepared take in the first letter, so it goes inside them

parts.note: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel

indicators.note: onset means the start, so only the first letter of water is used

parts.note: on can mean ready or set to go, as a performer is on

explanation.surface: A submarine sailor gets ready to take on water during a dark spell.
explanation.definitionFit: The lunar phase when the moon is invisible, giving the darkest nights of the month.

clue.text: Cracked head? Totally gutted

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the first and last letters of totally

explanation.surface: Someone with a split skull is completely devastated.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for mad or crazy.

clue.text: Expert smothers company junior in praise

indicators.note: the expert covers and encloses the other pieces, so they go inside it

parts.note: an ace is an expert
a lad is a young boy

explanation.surface: A senior specialist heaps acclaim on a firm's trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an accolade is an expression of high praise or an honour.

clue.text: Retired hurt, perhaps, in unlikely situation

definitions.meaning: in cricket a batsman who retires hurt walks off injured, having gone from the pitch
unconventional or out of the blue, from the baseball area far from the batter

explanation.surface: An injured player withdrawing seems a strange turn of events.
explanation.walkthrough: Retired hurt is a cricket term for a batsman leaving the game through injury.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is having quit the pitch; the other is the idiom for unexpected or unorthodox.

clue.text: I note main item in issue now available

parts.note: the main is the open sea
issue means offspring, and a son is one of them

explanation.surface: Someone notes that the main point in a question is now settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: produce that is ripe and on sale at its proper time of year.

clue.text: Loved ones, cross, rebuffed attempt to interview?

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so both words are read backwards

parts.note: pets are loved animals, or a term for darlings
a rood is a cross or crucifix

explanation.surface: Family members, irritated, turn away a reporter seeking a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists' jargon: to waylay someone at their front entrance for a comment.

clue.text: Legendary musician: King and he appearing separately in musical work

indicators.note: he is placed inside the musical work as well
the king and he go into the work at different points rather than together

parts.note: an opus is a musical composition
R is rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A mythic minstrel performs a piece where a monarch and another man each take a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing separately' means the two inserted pieces are not side by side: one lands after the first letter of the work, the other after its second.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the lyre player of Greek myth who went into the underworld for Eurydice.

clue.text: Look cross, initially faced with seats some way back?

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of faced is taken

parts.note: row N is a row of seats a long way from the front in a theatre

explanation.surface: Someone scowls at first when given seats far from the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to scowl or knit the brows in displeasure.

clue.text: Old negative quality about love is generating unease

indicators.note: the negative quality goes around love

parts.note: a minus is a drawback or negative point
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An ancient flaw in a relationship is causing anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: threatening or foreboding, so making people uneasy.

clue.text: Prince with payment reduced prior to conflict

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a reward is a payment for a service

explanation.surface: A royal accepts a smaller fee before hostilities begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes the period before a war, especially the Second World War.

clue.text: Souvenir article retaining little power — a facsimile

indicators.note: the souvenir holds on to the small piece, so it goes inside

parts.note: a relic is a keepsake from the past
P is the abbreviation for power
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A memento with little force is just a copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an exact copy or reproduction.

clue.text: Religion is supported by priest, though not entirely

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes after
not entirely means the priest word loses its last letter

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: A faith is backed by a cleric, if only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the monotheistic faith of Muslims.

clue.text: Rotten set of products not appearing on the Net?

parts.note: food gone off is rotten
a line is a range of goods a company sells

explanation.surface: A poor range of goods is missing from the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Disconnected from the internet, so absent from it.

clue.text: Wide support for boot or other part of car

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
a heel supports the back of a boot

explanation.surface: A broad strut holds up a car's luggage compartment or some other bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boot' looks like the car's luggage space, but it is footwear; the car comes back in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of the round parts a car rolls on, besides the boot.

clue.text: Unusually clear — having some sense in committing crime

indicators.note: unusually suggests the letters of clear set out in an odd order

parts.note: nous is common sense or gumption

explanation.surface: Something oddly obvious shows a bit of wit in a criminal act.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is larceny, so the adjective describes someone engaged in that offence.

clue.text: Clooney, perhaps, revolted by misbehaviour of army

parts.note: to rise up is to revolt

indicators.note: misbehaviour suggests the letters of army acting out of order

explanation.surface: George Clooney, perhaps, is disgusted by soldiers behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaviour of' rearranges ARMY as MARY. The surface points to George; the answer is the singer, his aunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the American singer of that name, aunt of the actor George Clooney.

clue.text: Scientist is probing connection after setback

indicators.note: is pokes into the other piece, so it goes inside
a setback sends the word for connection backwards

parts.note: a node is a junction or connecting point

explanation.surface: A researcher investigates a link after a reversal of fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Thomas Edison, the American inventor of the phonograph and light-bulb pioneer.
